assumptions: H is a Hermitian Hamiltonian on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space; the canonical ensemble is specified by H and inverse temperature beta.
This is a state definition, not a claim that arbitrary open-system dynamics equilibrates to it.
variables: rho_beta: normalized canonical density operator; H: system Hamiltonian.
beta = 1/(k_B T): inverse energy for the positive-temperature regime; Z: partition function.
patches.regime: Finite-dimensional canonical ensemble at T > 0. Infinite-dimensional use additionally requires a finite partition function; a reduced interacting state need not be the Gibbs state of its bare Hamiltonian.
patches.units: H and k_B T have energy units, beta has inverse-energy units, and beta H, Z and rho_beta are dimensionless.
patches.theoryRelationship: Canonical state used to initialize the source-qualified quantum work identity; existing review provenance is retained.

sourceLocations.locator: Sec. 2.1, printed/PDF pp. 1–2, Eq. (2.1) and partition function immediately following it.
Sec. II.C, printed/PDF p. 8: weak-coupling condition and discussion that a reduced interacting Gibbs state need not have Gibbs form for the subsystem Hamiltonian.

assumptions: An initially canonical finite-dimensional system undergoes a fixed unitary driving protocol from H_i to H_f; the initial inverse temperature is beta.
W = E_m^f - E_n^i is work done on the system in the two-projective-energy-measurement distribution, not a generic single-time work observable.
variables: Angle brackets: average over p(n,m) = exp(-beta E_n^i) |<m_f|U|n_i>|^2 / Z_i.
Delta F = -(1/beta) ln(Z_f/Z_i): equilibrium free-energy difference at the same beta; the final actual state need not be thermal.
patches.regime: Closed-system quantum work identity under the stated protocol. Arbitrary initial states, feedback-conditioned protocols and arbitrary open channels require separate conditions or modified relations.
patches.units: W and Delta F have energy units; beta = 1/(k_B T), so both exponential arguments are dimensionless.
patches.theoryRelationship: Tasaki Eq. (2.7) with beta-tilde = beta gives the preserved equation; the existing review supplies the explicit two-measurement work convention.

sourceLocations.locator: Sec. 2.1–2.2, printed/PDF p. 2, Eqs. (2.4)–(2.7); set beta-tilde = beta in Eq. (2.7).
Sec. V.A, printed/PDF p. 21, Eqs. (16)–(20): joint energy-measurement statistics, work, free energy and equality.

assumptions: The ln 2 specialization refers to resetting an initially unbiased classical bit (or maximally mixed qubit) to a fixed pure logical state.
The reservoir initially has a Gibbs state at T > 0, is uncorrelated with the memory, and memory plus reservoir undergo unitary evolution with all relevant resources included.
variables: Q: average heat deposited in the reservoir, positive for an increase of its energy.
k_B: Boltzmann constant; T: initial reservoir temperature; ln 2: one-bit entropy decrease measured in nats.
patches.regime: Lower-bound inequality, not an equality. Biased or incomplete erasure uses the actual entropy decrease instead of ln 2. Exact pure reset from a full-rank state is impossible with a finite-dimensional finite-temperature reservoir; the displayed ideal reset cost is a limiting benchmark, not automatic finite-bath attainability.
patches.units: Q and k_B T have energy units. Natural logarithms are used; information entropy is dimensionless here.
patches.theoryRelationship: One-bit specialization of the source-qualified entropy-decrease bound; existing review provenance is retained. It is not a universal cost for every logical operation.
